newsitem.title: ITALY: Dini's party suggests changes to Italy "Euro-tax".
newsitem.headline: Dini's party suggests changes to Italy "Euro-tax".

text.p: Italian Renewal, the centrist party led by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, on Wednesday unveiled a series of alternative tax measures to those contained in the centre-left government's controversial budgetary "Euro-tax".

Ottaviano Del Turco, the party's leader in the Senate (upper house), told a news conference the proposals were intended to "make the government more forthcoming" on the deeply unpopular levy designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire ($8.3 billion).
Italian Renewal, a member of the government, suggested scrapping a tax on severance pay intended to raise 3.5 trillion lire and raising one trillion lire through a corporate tax.

The remaining 2.5 trillion lire could be raised partly with "an extra effort on the revenue side" and partly by levying a one-off charge on early-retirement pensions for people under the age of 50 to 52, Del Turco said.

Italian Renewal, which earlier said it wanted to see the "sacrifices" of the Euro-tax shared out more fairly, also proposed changes to income tax measures which the government had planned to use to raise 5.5 trillion lire.

It suggested levying a flat rate on all earnings above 20 million lire a year, instead of the government's current proposal which has a separate threshold for the self-employed and a series of potential exemptions to the tax.
Del Turco said the 5.5 trillion lire figure would be reached by "extending the tax base down".
He said the party would present its amendments by 1900 GMT on Wednesday and discussions could then begin between parliamentary party leaders and the government.

A deadline of 1900 GMT has been set for budget amendments to be submitted. The opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance opposes the Euro-tax and the rest of the package, which aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire from next year's deficit.

Cesare Salvi, Senate leader of the Democratic Party (PDS) of the Left, earlier told reporters the government planned to unveil changes of its own to the Euro-tax at 1900 GMT. The PDS is the biggest party in Prodi's government.
